My name is Josh. I am a 35-year-old entrepreneur living on the Space Coast of Florida. I am an agnostic atheist, although I have always been fascinated by religion and studied Christianity and Judaism in depth before looking to the East for more answers. I started on reddit, on /r/koans and I kept at it for years. I came here to voat once Chairman Pao started raising a ruckus over there, but that is a story for another day.

My life is a hot mess, filled with bad habits and human failings. If I compare myself to the "average", I suppose I'm doing pretty well. However, one thing I've learned is that we must never compare ourselves to anyone else, only to our own past selves, and potential future selves. You may notice that I'm pretty hard on myself. I come from the "get over it" school of thought, and I despise any flavor of the "victim" mentality.

Anyway, one of the vices that I have struggled with for a long time is the joy of smoking. It's really great. I spend hundreds of dollars per month so I can fill my lungs with tar, slowly kill myself, smell gross, and fill every outfit I own with tons of tiny little burn holes. I would say the only vice better than smoking would be kicking oneself repeatedly in the balls, if such a thing were anatomically possible.

Back around 2011 or so, I quit smoking seriously (for the first time of many). I needed a new "habit" to replace my morning cigarette, and so, I started transcribing koans instead. After transcribing these koans, I do a yoga routine, and then I meditate, and then I go do my daily exercise.

The challenging thing about life is, unlike movies, it doesn't fade to black and roll credits. It just kinda...keeps going... until one day it doesn't. My story didn't end when I quit smoking. It didn't end when I lost 70 pounds. It didn't end when my business started doing better. It just keeps on going. And my story didn't end when I started smoking again, quit again, and started again. It didn't end when I gained back 20 pounds. It didn't end when my business nearly failed a few years ago, or when I almost got divorced last year. It just keeps on going.

I'm really babbling here, but perhaps it is useful to someone. I have achieved more in the past few years than I ever thought myself capable of, and I have also failed and stumbled and made mistake after mistake after stupid mistake. It just keeps on going.

I have in me the capability to become a better version of myself- a better Josh. You also have that capability, whatever your name might be. And I hope these koans can bring insight, and humor, and more than anything, a reminder that our human challenges are not unique, and that these zen masters were fighting the same human condition thousands of years ago. It just keeps going...

So that's enough babbling for one day. Ironically, in trying to cheer up a stranger on the Internet, I have instead cheered myself up. I'm going to extinguish this smoke, go stretch and meditate, and then I am going to listen to heavy metal and toss some weights around. My inner demons still chase me, but I wouldn't trade them for anything in the world.

Stay hungry, my fellow monastics. Make today count.
